transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… hi. I guess I’m here because my eating’s gotten kind of out of hand, especially after work. I’m a cashier, and after my shifts I’ll stop and buy takeout—probably more than I should, like burgers, fries, chicken, desserts… enough for a few people, honestly—and then I end up eating almost all of it myself before I go home. I know that sounds bad, I’m sorry, but I thought I should maybe talk to someone about it.
Do you feel guilty after eating all that food by yourself?

I mean… yeah, I guess I don’t feel great about it. I try not to make a huge deal out of it, because I know people overeat sometimes, but afterward I’m usually kind of embarrassed and mad at myself. Like, “why did I do that again?” Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you usually eat this much when you're not stressed or upset after work?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really paid attention to it that way. I guess I notice it more after work, but I don’t know if it’s always because I’m stressed or upset, if that makes sense. Sometimes it just sort of… happens. Is that an okay answer?
Do you think you eat more when you're feeling stressed or upset?

I… I don’t know for sure. I mean, stress might be part of it sometimes, yeah, but I haven’t really kept track or anything. It’s not like I can always point to one feeling and say, “that’s why.” Sometimes I’m just… tired, or I stop for food and then it kind of goes from there. Is that answering it okay?
Do you think eating helps you feel better when you're stressed or upset?

I’m not really sure. Maybe for a little bit it’s like… distracting, I guess, but I don’t know if I’d say it makes me feel better exactly. I haven’t really thought about it in that way. Is that what you mean?
Do you eat when you're feeling upset, even if you're not hungry?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but a lot of the time I’m not really hungry when it starts. Like even if I already had dinner with my wife, I’ll still end up looking around for something to eat. It’s like I’m trying to shut my head off for a while, I guess. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you think eating helps you escape or avoid thinking about your feelings?

Yeah… I think that’s probably a fair way to put it. I don’t know if I’m, like, consciously deciding that, but most of the time I’m not even hungry when it starts. Especially if I already ate dinner with my wife, I’ll still end up looking for something, and it’s kind of like I’m trying to shut my head off for a bit. Does that make sense?
How often do you have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time?

Um… I guess more than I’d like to admit. For the last several months it’s been, like, three or four nights most weeks. I don’t mean every single night, but… since the foreclosure calls started, I honestly can’t remember a week where it didn’t happen at least once. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started on those nights when you eat a large amount of food?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say I can, but on those nights it doesn’t really feel that way. Once I take that first bite, it’s like something in me kind of clicks off. I’ll be telling myself, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” but my hands just keep going for the next thing. It sounds bad saying it like that, but… that’s what it feels like.
Do you think your eating is more of a reaction to emotional stress or just a habitual behavior after work?

I think it’s more the stress, honestly… though maybe it’s kind of become a habit too. But most of the time I’m not even hungry when it starts. Like, I can have dinner with my wife and still later I’m looking around for food anyway. It feels less like I need food and more like I’m trying to quiet everything in my head for a little while, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating on those nights when you eat a large amount of food?

Not really, no… I mean, I’m embarrassed to say that because I know how it sounds. But once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me clicks off, and even if I’m telling myself, Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more, my hands just keep reaching for the next thing. It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it the way I should be, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself from continuing to eat once you've started eating a large amount of food?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the best way to put it. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m totally helpless, but in the moment, once I’ve started, it really does feel like I can’t stop myself. Like I’ll be thinking, “Demetrius, come on, you don’t need any more,” and still my hand is already reaching for the next thing. It’s embarrassing, but… yeah, that’s what happens.
Do you feel like you're eating much more quickly than usual during those episodes?

I’m… not totally sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid close attention to how fast I’m eating. It probably doesn’t feel normal in the moment, but I don’t know if I could say it’s much faster than usual. Sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you usually feel guilty or disgusted with yourself after these episodes of eating a large amount of food?

I don’t know if I’d use words that strong every time… I mean, I definitely don’t feel good about it afterward. I usually kind of wish I hadn’t done it and try not to think about it too much. But “disgusted” sounds… harsh, I guess. Maybe sometimes, but I’m not totally sure how to answer that right.
Do you feel like you're unable to control how much you eat during those episodes?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t like saying it that way, because it makes me sound like I’m not trying, but once I take that first bite, it’s like something in me kind of clicks off. I’ll be telling myself, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” and somehow my hands just keep reaching for the next thing anyway. Does that make sense?
Do you usually eat a large amount of food within a short period of time, like less than two hours?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say. After my shifts, I’ll sometimes buy way more takeout than one person really needs—burgers, fries, chicken, desserts, stuff like that—and I’ll sit in my car or somewhere and eat most of it before I even go home. It’s… usually not spread out over the whole night or anything. It’s pretty quick, like within an hour or two. I know that sounds like a lot.
